key_insight: TrajectoryFlowNet learns both how particles move and the flow field carrying them from very limited trajectory measurements. Its physics-informed approach connects individual particle paths with the surrounding fluid motion.
problem_solved: Reconstructing flow fields and predicting long-range particle trajectories when only sparse measurements of particle motion are available.
method: Combine Lagrangian learning of particle trajectories with Eulerian learning of flow fields.
Use physics-informed learning to jointly predict particle paths and fluid motion from limited trajectory measurements.
Validate the approach in simulations and blood-flow experiments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, the work illustrates how physical knowledge can support learning from sparse observations. Joint trajectory and flow prediction could help analyze fluid systems where extensive measurements are difficult to obtain.
visual_elements: Sparse measured particle positions expanding into predicted long-range paths.
A split diagram contrasting particle-following Lagrangian and fixed-location Eulerian perspectives.
A flow-field map with arrows overlaid by particle trajectories.
Side-by-side panels representing simulation and blood-flow validation.
paper_title: Lagrangian–Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
paper_authors: Jingdi Wan, Hongping Wang, Bo Liu, Xiaolei Yang, Xiaodong Hu
